slides.title: Introduction to U-Net
bullet_points: U-Net is a popular architecture for image segmentation tasks.
Consists of an encoder and a decoder path.
Encoder captures features at different scales.
Decoder reconstructs the image, refining details.

slides.title: Why Skip Connections?
bullet_points: Skip connections allow the model to retain spatial information.
Prevent information loss during the upsampling process.
Combine low-level feature maps with high-level semantic information.
Enhance the ability to segment small and fine structures.
slides.code_snippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class UNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(UNet, self).__init__()
        # Encoder layers
        self.encoder1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.encoder2 = nn.Conv2d(64, 128, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        # Decoder layers
        self.decoder1 = nn.ConvTranspose2d(128, 64, kernel_size=2, stride=2)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.encoder1(x)
        skip = x
        x = self.encoder2(x)
        x = self.decoder1(x)
        x = torch.cat([x, skip], dim=1)
        return x

slides.title: Skip Connections Mechanism
bullet_points: Skip connections concatenate feature maps from encoder and decoder paths.
Example: torch.cat([decoder_layer, encoder_layer], dim=1)
Preserve spatial information by combining low-level features with high-level semantics.
Enhance the model’s ability to capture fine details.
slides.code_snippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

def apply_skip_connection(decoder_layer, encoder_layer):
    return torch.cat([decoder_layer, encoder_layer], dim=1)

# Example usage
skip_connection = apply_skip_connection(torch.randn(1, 64, 128, 128), torch.randn(1, 64, 128, 128))
assert skip_connection.shape == (1, 128, 128, 128)

slides.title: Practical Application: Skin Lesion Segmentation
bullet_points: Skin lesions often have complex boundaries requiring detailed segmentation.
U-Net with skip connections effectively captures both coarse and fine details.
Skip connections help in retaining important spatial features.
Improved segmentation accuracy for medical applications.
slides.code_snippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class UNetForSkinLesion(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(UNetForSkinLesion, self).__init__()
        self.encoder1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.encoder2 = nn.Conv2d(64, 128, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.decoder1 = nn.ConvTranspose2d(128, 64, kernel_size=2, stride=2)
        self.final_conv = nn.Conv2d(128, 1, kernel_size=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.encoder1(x)
        skip = x
        x = self.encoder2(x)
        x = self.decoder1(x)
        x = torch.cat([x, skip], dim=1)
        x = self.final_conv(x)
        return x

# Test the model
model = UNetForSkinLesion()
dummy_input = torch.randn(1, 1, 256, 256)
output = model(dummy_input)
assert output.shape == (1, 1, 256, 256)
